title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the 1982 'formulaire' for the lifted modular groups in genus 1. It continues the previous page, which set up the 1981 dictionary between π_{0,3}, SL(2,Z) and GL(2,Z).

(1) The extension. Grothendieck considers 1 → Z →(k) GL(2,Z)~ → GL(2,Z) → 1. Its restriction over SL(2,Z) is the central extension SL(2,Z)~. The Z is the kernel of the universal-cover-type extension. GL(2,Z) acts on the kernel through det ∈ {±1}, so k(Z) is central in SL~ but not in GL~. GL(2,Z) also acts on SL(2,Z)~ by conjugation by any lift; this action does not extend to GL~.

(2) Generators of SL~. Put l'_0 := k(1). He chooses lifts ρ~ of ρ (order 6 below), σ~ of σ (order 4 below) and ω~_0 of ω_0 = -1, subject to ρ~^{-3} = σ~^2 = ω~_0. Then ρ~^6 = l'_0^{-1} and σ~^4 = ω~_0^2 = l'_0.

(3) Braid presentation. Set ε~_0 = σ~ρ~ and ε~_1 = ρ~ε~_0ρ~^{-1} = σ~ε~_0σ~^{-1} = ρ~σ~. Then:
- ε~_1ε~_0 = ρ~^{-1};
- σ~ = ε~_0ε~_1ε~_0 = ε~_1ε~_0ε~_1.
So SL(2,Z)~ = <ε_0, ε_1 | ε_0ε_1ε_0 = ε_1ε_0ε_1> = B_3 (boxed on the page). In braid language:
- σ~ = Δ (Garside element);
- ω~_0 = Δ^2 = (ε_1ε_0)^3 generates the centre;
- l'_0 = Δ^4 generates ker(B_3 → SL(2,Z)).

(4) The orientation-reversing lift. A lift τ~' = r~_0 of τ' (the matrix [[0,1],[1,0]]) can be chosen to be an involution. It acts by ρ~ ↦ ρ~^{-1}, σ~ ↦ σ~^{-1}, ε~_0 ↦ ε~_1^{-1}, ε~_1 ↦ ε~_0^{-1}, and l'_0 ↦ l'_0^{-1}. Hence GL(2,Z)~ = B_3 ⋊ Z/2.

With r~_1 = ρ~^{-1}r~_0 and r~_∞ = σ~r~_0 (all three involutions), this gives a presentation by three involutions. The intended relation is (r_0r_1)^3 = (r_0r_∞)^2, i.e. ρ~^3σ~^2 = 1 with ρ~ = r_0r_1 and σ~ = r_∞r_0. This lifts GL(2,Z) = D_6 *_{D_2} D_4 from the previous page.

(5) Indexed generators. For i ∈ Z/3 = {0,1,∞}:
- ε~_{i+1} = ρ~ε~_iρ~^{-1} and l~_i = ε~_i^2;
- σ~_i satisfies σ~_i^2 = ω~_0 and σ~_i^4 = l'_0;
- ε~_i = σ~_{i-1}ρ~ = ρ~σ~_{i+1}.
The key relation is l~_∞ l~_1 l~_0 = ω~_0. With λ~_i = ω~_0^{-1} l~_i this becomes λ~_∞λ~_1λ~_0 = ω~_0^{-2} = l'_0^{-1}. This lifts the SL(2,Z) relation λ_∞λ_1λ_0 = 1 from the previous page; the lifting now produces an anomaly l'_0.

(6) Where it leads. The next page realises these elements as automorphisms of the free group <u,v>, i.e. π_1 of the once-holed torus.

Purpose: build the genus-1 piece of the Teichmüller tower with the boundary/tangential twist included. Concretely this is π_1 of M_{1,1} with a tangent vector (which is B_3), plus its extension by complex conjugation / orientation reversal. Here the kernel Z behaves like Z(1), the det-twisted module. This is needed for the 'Lego' gluing of the (1,1) piece to the (0,3)/(0,4) pieces.
errors: The relation line '(r_1 r_0)^3 (r_0 r_∞)^2 = 1' is consistent with ρ~^3σ~^2 = 1 only with orientation conventions ρ~ = r_0r_1 and σ~ = r_∞r_0. With r_1r_0 = ρ~^{-1} (as on the previous page, Γ_1Γ_0 = λ_∞ = ρ^{-1}), one should read (r_0r_1)^3 = (r_0r_∞)^2, or (r_1r_0)^{-3}(r_0r_∞)^2 = 1. This is a minor sign/ordering slip; in GL(2,Z) itself both versions hold because both sides equal -1, but they differ in the lift.
Notational slip: tildes are dropped in places, e.g. 'τ'^2 = 1', 'σ~(ε_0)', 'ρ(ε~_i)', 'σ_{i+1}'. These are harmless.

Checked as correct: σ~ = ε_0ε_1ε_0 = ε_1ε_0ε_1; ε~_1ε~_0 = ρ~^{-1}; and l~_∞l~_1l~_0 = Δ^2. The last was verified by matrix computation (the product is -1 in SL(2,Z)) and by the degree count in the abelianization of B_3 (degree 6 on both sides), and λ~_∞λ~_1λ~_0 = l'_0^{-1} follows.

ideas.what: SL(2,Z)~ (central Z-extension of SL(2,Z)) is the braid group B_3, with lifts of the transvections satisfying the braid relation; ω~_0 = Δ^2 is central and l'_0 = Δ^4 generates the kernel
ideas.modern_name: B_3 ≅ SL(2,Z)~ ≅ π_1 of the space of elliptic curves with a nonzero tangent vector (C^2 minus the discriminant) ≅ mapping class group of the once-holed torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Artin; the trefoil-knot-group description; Milnor's 'Introduction to algebraic K-theory' for the universal central extension)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the genus-1 (1,1) Teichmüller group; the explicit B_3 presentation does not appear there as far as I know

ideas.what: The extension of GL(2,Z) by Z with GL acting on Z through det (non-central), split by an orientation-reversing involution acting by ε_0 ↦ ε_1^{-1}, ε_1 ↦ ε_0^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Extended mapping class group Mod^±(S_{1,1}) ≅ B_3 ⋊ Z/2; the kernel twisted by det is analogous to Z(1) under complex conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (mapping class group literature); the Galois analogue appears in Ihara and Nakamura's work on GT acting on B_3

ideas.what: Presentation of GL(2,Z)~ by three involutions r_0, r_1, r_∞ with (r_0r_1)^3 = (r_0r_∞)^2, lifting the (2,3,∞)-type amalgam D_6 *_{D_2} D_4
ideas.modern_name: Generation of extended mapping class groups by involutions / reflection-type presentation of Mod^±(S_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; involution generation of mapping class groups studied later by others

ideas.what: Lifting the triangle relation λ_∞λ_1λ_0 = 1 to B_3 gives the anomaly l'_0^{-1}, via the identity ε_∞^2ε_1^2ε_0^2 = Δ^2 with indices permuted cyclically by ρ~
ideas.modern_name: Relation among squared Dehn twists in the once-holed torus mapping class group; the boundary twist appears as an anomaly

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly records that the reflection (complex-conjugation) lift acts on the kernel Z through det, so the kernel behaves as a Tate-twisted Z(1). He sets up a symmetric Z/3-indexed formulaire (ε_i, σ_i, l_i, λ_i) for the genus-1 tangential Teichmüller group. This is a well-organised working document for the (1,1) building block of the Teichmüller tower, but the content is standard.
missed.quote: k(Z) central dans Sl(2,Z)~ mais non dans Gl(2,Z)~ ... Gl(2,Z) opère sur Z ... par multiplication par dét u ∈ {±1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's 1982 bookkeeping of the genus-1 piece with real structure, which is of historical interest for the genesis of the Esquisse's Teichmüller tower. There is no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful, correct computations identifying SL(2,Z)~ with B_3 and GL(2,Z)~ with B_3 ⋊ Z/2. They are standard facts, here organised in Grothendieck's symmetric Z/3-indexed notation for the Teichmüller tower. Historically interesting as a working step, but nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'conditions [?] ρ~, σ~, ω~_0 ainsi :' likely reads 'Conditions liant ρ~, σ~, ω~_0 ainsi :'.
'par l'entremise du [?] de dét u' plausibly reads 'par l'entremise du caractère dét u', i.e. via det, multiplication by det u ∈ {±1}.
In the GL(2,Z)~ block the image reads 'Gl(2,Z)~' (the '4' in the image is a malformed 2).
The second line should read ε~_1 = ρ~(ε~_0) = σ~^{-1}(ε~_0) = σ~(ε~_0) = ρ~σ~, with tildes on ε_0.
'ρ(σ~_i) = σ~_{i+1} = l~_{i-1}ε~_{i+1}' — the ρ is meant as ρ~ (conjugation).
